beatOutlines.textOutline: Watching fifteen-minute red and green candles thrash about, Raju gets utterly disoriented.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Sharma ji strips away time and volume noise from his screen, pulling up a Point and Figure chart.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Raju notices that the screen displays only crisp columns of X's and O's.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Mistaking a noisy wick for a real breakout on the bar chart, Raju bought at ₹640 in haste.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Moments later price plummeted to ₹615, while on the P&F chart it was merely routine consolidation.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: First rule of Point and Figure: time does not exist; only pure price movement is recorded.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: In Murphy's Chapter 11, we enter the distinct domain of Point and Figure charting.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: We will explore how X and O columns are drafted and master the discipline of 3-box reversals.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: And finally, we will master the art of projecting precise price targets via the Horizontal Count.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Traditional bar charts are time-based, printing a new bar every session regardless of price movement.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: On a Point and Figure chart, X represents rising demand and O denotes falling supply; they never share a column.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Its supreme virtue is total objectivity: displaying the unadulterated tug-of-war between demand and supply.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Constructing a Point and Figure chart requires defining two critical parameters: Box Size and Reversal Amount.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: If the box size is five rupees, price must move a full five rupees before plotting a new X; fractions are ignored.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Incomplete increments are disregarded entirely, guaranteeing that only genuine price milestones are captured.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The 3-box reversal method is the industry benchmark, filtering out minor counter-trend ripples cleanly.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: If the stock is at ₹650, price must retreat by at least ₹15 to justify opening an O column.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: A decline of only ₹10 leaves the chart unchanged; this buffer provides near-total immunity from whipsaws.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: While bar chart trendlines follow arbitrary angles, P&F trendlines are strictly drawn at 45 degrees.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Because grid boxes are square, a 45-degree line represents the precise mathematical balance of price and column.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: As long as price stays above the bullish support line, sell signals are ignored and only buy breakouts are taken.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The foundational P&F patterns are the Double Top and Double Bottom, vastly cleaner than bar chart equivalents.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Crucial distinction: on bar charts a double top is bearish, but in P&F a double top is a bullish breakout over the prior peak.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Likewise in a double bottom breakdown, the moment an O column drops one box below the prior O, a confirmed sell triggers.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: The Horizontal Count for Price Targets
scenes.concept: The Horizontal Count for Price Targets

beatOutlines.textOutline: The most celebrated edge of P&F charting is projecting precise price targets using the Horizontal Count.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The formula is simple: count columns across the base, multiply by 3 and box size, and add to the pattern floor.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Murphy highlights: the wider the base, the further the move; the law of cause and effect in full display.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

takeaways: The Horizontal Count for Price Targets

beatOutlines.textOutline: Now your turn. Analyze this Point and Figure technical scenario.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Think... recall the rules governing box size and the 3-box reversal threshold.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: A minimum drop of ₹15 is required, and 3 O's will appear simultaneously at ₹645, ₹640, and ₹635!
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Raju sets up a Point and Figure grid on his terminal and writes in his journal.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Sharma ji reinforces the core practical rule of Point and Figure execution.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Raju smiles and confirms he will never get trapped by the noise of bar charts again.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Let us summarize the comprehensive principles of Chapter 11 Part 1 across eight key steps.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Columns of X's track advancing demand while O columns measure seller pressure.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The 3-box reversal parameter filters out minor retracements, shielding you from false chops.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The 45-degree trendline mathematically establishes the dominant supply/demand channel.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: And the Horizontal Count measures base width to project future price objectives with pinpoint accuracy.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Remember: When time is eliminated from the chart, only the pure truth of price remains.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

summarySteps: Point & Figure completely eliminates the time and volume axes
Columns alternate strictly between rising X's and falling O's
Box Size defines the minimum price threshold required to plot an entry
3-Box Reversal requires three full boxes to trigger an opposite column
Minor counter-trend noise is filtered out, preventing intraday whipsaws
Trendlines are strictly drawn at 45-degree angles on square grids
P&F Double Top is an objective breakout buy, not a bearish top
Horizontal Count projects vertical price targets from base width
bottomTakeaway: Discipline and grounded market understanding are essential for survival.
